news.title: mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory allocator for the modern era
news.summary_raw:
mimalloc is an open-source, modern, scalable memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free. It is relatively small (~12K lines), with clear internal data structures, and is easy to build and integrate into other projects. It provides bounded worst-case allocation times (up to OS primitives), bounded space overhead, low internal fragmentation, and minimal contention by relying almost exclusively on atomic operations.
The post mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released mimalloc, a high-performance, open-source memory allocator that replaces malloc and free, featuring bounded worst-case allocation times, low internal fragmentation, and minimal contention. This gives developers a drop-in replacement for memory management that is relatively small, easy to build, and integrates well into other projects.
news.enterprise_use: Note this for potential use in internal projects that require high-performance, low-latency memory allocation. While primarily aimed at general software development, this may be of indirect interest to IT engineers for optimizing specific tasks but requires further evaluation.

The industry has invested enormously in the first.
